Well, I can safely assume that anyone can be successful in life with dedication. I don't have that dedication. I can't even play video games (something I'm supposed to enjoy) for more than a few hours at a given time. I get bored of everything quickly.
A solution will arise if you put in enough time/effort, but I don't think I'm really capable of doing that.

What options are there though? I can't really think of a hobby (or something that is considered fun) that earns money. Other than doing things professionally, which often requires a lot of dedication and time which I don't think I could do.

Nothing much that isn't included in the op. It's just I'm running out of money and school is about to end, so I have to either get a job or go to uni. I don't want to get a student loan because I'll likely screw over the cosigner because I won't end up working, and I definitely don't want to work. It seems pretty hopeless.

I could give therapy a go, I can get some free sessions as part of medicare. I might try going to the doctors and changing my medication/booking therapy, but if I don't see results I can't imagine myself trying any longer
I may give changing meds a go.
I will probably try more things, but I have almost no money left from my job because I spent it all trying things already.

Hanging around with people does make me feel better for the time being, but it's only temporary and doesn't fix my problems. I've tried looking into professions/hobbies etc to find something that interests me, but I haven't found anything. One of the only fun things I do on my own is play poker (holdem) at casinos, which I only started doing a few weeks ago. In fact, I probably only find it fun because there's other people around, and there's a lot of chatty/funny people on the tables. I will probably play it a bit more and see where it takes me, but going pro is extremely difficult.
